back: Producing output at the lowest possible average total cost: the lowest point of the ATC curve, where MC = ATC.
Resources are allocated to the goods consumers value most; with no externalities it occurs where price = marginal cost.

front: State the conditions for productive and allocative efficiency.
back: Productive: MC = ATC (minimum ATC). Allocative: P = MC (generally marginal social benefit = marginal social cost).
Obtaining the maximum output from a given set of inputs.
Improvements in efficiency over time through innovation, new products and investment.
Costs above the minimum possible because weak competition lets managers and workers become slack.
A situation in which no one can be made better off without making someone else worse off.

front: Is a perfectly competitive firm efficient in the long run?
back: Yes, productively and allocatively: price falls to minimum ATC and equals MC. It is weak on dynamic efficiency because it earns only normal profit.
It sets MR = MC, which gives a price above MC and output below the efficient level, creating a welfare loss.
